Page 1/6 
Machine Learning (BMI/GEO/WNA) 
Code Assignment U1A1  
Linear Regression 
This is NOT a group Assignment. 
 
10 marks 
Please complete seeing the videos for Week 1-2 before attempting this 
assignment.  
 
Use real estate valuation regression dataset : 
https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/477/real+estate+valuation+data+set  from 
the UCI repository, and use google colab to code. 
 
First, download the csv file, and open it in your computer and analyze the data. 
Try to understand what the data is about. Read through the data description 
given 
in 
the 
UCI 
website 
as 
well. 
 
Section A 
Answer the following questions [1 mark if you answer all the below questions] 
: 
1. How many samples are there? 
<<   414      >> 
2. How 
many 
input 
variables 
are 
there? 
<<   6   >> 
3. Which 
column 
is 
the 
output 
variable 
(target 
outcome)? 
<<   y house price of unit area   >> 
4. What does each of the input columns mean ? 
<<   transaction date, house age, distance  to the nearest MRT station, 
number of convenience stores, latitude, longitude  >> 
 
Section B

Page 2/6 
For each of the questions below, you need to put in the screenshot of the code 
and its output. You could use the sample google colab file that is provided with 
this assignment. 
 
1. Understanding the dataset [4 marks] 
There are many input variables in this dataset. Use only X1 to X4 as input 
variables, and y as the output variable. 
Using the scatter plots between each of the input features (X1-X4) and the 
output (Y), which input variable, do you think, is better in predicting the output 
/ target variable ? 
 
plt.scatter(x1,y,color='red') 
plt.title('House Price vs Transaction Date') 
plt.xlabel('Transaction Date') 
plt.ylabel('House Price') 
plt.show() 
 
 
 
 
plt.scatter(x2,y,color='green') 
plt.title('House Price vs House Age') 
plt.xlabel('House Age') 
plt.ylabel('House Price') 
plt.show()

Page 3/6 
 
plt.scatter(x3,y,color='cyan') 
plt.title('House Price vs Distance to the nearest MRT station') 
plt.xlabel('Distance to the nearest MRT station') 
plt.ylabel('House Price') 
plt.show() 
 
 
 
 
 
plt.scatter(x4,y) 
plt.title('House Price vs Number of convenient stores') 
plt.xlabel('Number of convenient stores') 
plt.ylabel('House Price') 
plt.show()

Page 4/6 
 
 
 
 
<< Distance to the nearest MRT station: This can better predict the model 
because most of the samples are clustered together in the beginning of the 
plot and also showing a negative trend. As the distance from the metro station 
increases, house price decreases. 
 
House age: In this also there is a negative trend for most part of the plot. As 
the house age increases, house price decreases. But when compared to the 
above case, samples are not that much clustered , somewhat spreaded. 
 
Number of convenient stores: During most part of the plot, a slight upward  
trend is showing. >> 
 
2. Write code to find out how many samples are there in total in this dataset? [1 
mark] 
 
  
 
3. What is the train test split ratio that you have chosen ? [1 Mark]

Page 5/6 
 
 
<<   The train test split ratio selected is 70:30   >> 
 
4. Evaluate the linear regression model by computing the MAE, MSE and Mean 
Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) . 
(for MAPE - pls refer to the sample here - https://scikit-
learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.metrics.mean_absolute_percent
age_error.html)  
[3 marks]

Page 6/6 
 
 
 
5. What are the 3 new things that you learned after you completed this 
assignment ? 
• Learned to find out the trend, followed by the data points, from  
a scatter plot 
• Learned to train the model using more than one input variable 
• Learned to compare and evaluate different models
